story.iWant: REST API endpoints to check system health
story.soThat: I can monitor Megalith status and integrate with monitoring tools
story.tasks: - Add Flask/Dash server endpoints in src/web/dashboard/app.py - Read latest metrics files from data/metrics/ directory - Calculate health status from recent ETL metrics - Implement 5-minute caching for metrics responses - Create HealthStatus and MetricsSummary Pydantic models

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: - Given the Dash application is running, when I call GET /health, then I receive JSON response with: status (ok/degraded/down), timestamp, version, uptime - And status is "degraded" if >10% of last 10 ETL runs failed - And status is "down" if dashboard cannot read data files - Given the Dash application is running, when I call GET /metrics, then I receive JSON with: total_sources, total_items, last_etl_run_times, error_rates_per_source

artifacts.docs: <doc path="docs/prd.md" title="Product Requirements Document" section="Success Criteria" snippet="System Reliability target: 99%+ uptime for watchers and ETL pipelines, Failed ETL runs <1%, watcher downtime <1 hour/month"/>

artifact.reason: Main Dash application with Flask server where health API endpoints (/health, /metrics) need to be added to app.server
Existing metrics model that health API will read from to calculate system status and error rates
Method that saves metrics files to data/metrics/ directory which health API will read
Utility class for aggregating and processing metrics data for API responses (to be created)

constraints.constraint: Health API responses must be under 200ms (95th percentile)
Metrics API responses must be under 500ms (95th percentile)
Implement 5-minute TTL caching for both /health and /metrics endpoints
API endpoints must degrade gracefully if metrics files are corrupted or unreadable
Use existing Flask server from Dash framework (app.server) without additional server processes

interface.name: GET /health
interface.signature: GET /health -> {status: str, timestamp: str, version: str, uptime_seconds: float, etl_health?: dict}

interface.name: GET /metrics
interface.signature: GET /metrics?time_range=1h|24h|7d -> {total_sources: int, total_items: int, last_etl_runs: dict, error_rates: dict, avg_duration: dict}

interface.name: HealthStatus
interface.signature: class HealthStatus(BaseModel): status: str, timestamp: datetime, version: str, uptime_seconds: float

interface.name: MetricsSummary
interface.signature: class MetricsSummary(BaseModel): total_sources: int, total_items_processed: int, last_etl_runs: dict, error_rates: dict

tests.standards: API testing follows pytest framework with requests library for endpoint testing. Health status calculation tested with mock metrics files showing various failure rates. Performance testing ensures response times meet requirements (<200ms for /health, <500ms for /metrics).

ideas.idea: Test: Call GET /health endpoint and verify response structure matches HealthStatus model with status, timestamp, version, uptime fields
Test: Mock 10 ETL runs with 2 failures (20% failure rate) and verify status="degraded"
Test: Corrupt metrics files and verify /health returns status="down" gracefully
Test: Call GET /metrics endpoint and verify all required aggregations are present
Test: Load test both endpoints to verify <200ms for /health and <500ms for /metrics
Test: Verify 5-minute TTL cache by making multiple rapid calls and checking response timestamps
